passages.note: Overview page establishes his prime sponsorship but prints only the short title, which itself names five subjects.
The vote page names him and the count but no provision, and at 56-2 fewer than 10% voted against, so it is near-unanimous as well as a vote on a multi-subject act.

passages.provision_quote: Beginning in 2026, aT ANY VOTING LOCATION THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT, AND IF SO THE ELECTION OFFICIAL SHALL:
passages.note: The act amends nineteen statute sections covering polling places, sample ballots, early ballot requests, signature verification, provisional ballots, canvass deadlines, recounts and the primary election date, and its identification change is optional rather than required.

rows.reasoning: HB2785 (2024), which Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted for, is an omnibus election act amending nineteen statute sections from polling places and sample ballots through "canvass; recounts; ballots" and the 2024 primary date, so no single clause of it is his position (V4 multi-subject, and the vote is near-unanimous at 56-2). Its one identification change lets a voter "CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT" as an alternative to signature verification, which is optional and is not "Require photo ID in person and an ID number on every mail ballot"; the accepted-document list in section 16-579 is reprinted unchanged, so the act does not set what identification is required to vote. No passage survives V4, and an amendment to an existing ID law that does not set the required identification leaves the existing law's rung, not his position.
